analysis.investment_thesis: Solarium Green is a 2018-incorporated solar EPC company freshly listed on BSE at a P/E of 21.5 — well above my 15x ceiling and lacking the multi-year audited earnings track record I require. The profitability metrics are attractive, but without visibility into book value, current ratio, debt, or dividend history, there is no demonstrable margin of safety.
key_strengths: ROE of 23% and ROCE of 20.1% indicate genuine earning power on deployed capital
Promoter holding of 58.34% signals skin in the game and aligned incentives
Operates in a structurally growing sector (solar EPC/turnkey) with policy tailwinds
key_risks: P/E of 21.5 exceeds my 15x threshold — no margin of safety at INR 209
Incorporated 2018; lacks the 5+ year earnings record I demand — speculative by definition
EPC/civil construction is project-based, working-capital heavy, and cyclical — earnings quality unproven
red_flags: Recently listed SME-scale (INR 301 Cr mcap) — IPO premium priced by sellers, not buyers
No disclosed P/B, current ratio, debt-to-equity, or interest coverage — cannot verify balance sheet strength
No dividend history disclosed — unproven cash return to shareholders
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a strict Graham lens, this security fails the threshold tests before we even get to qualitative assessment. A P/E of 21.5 implies an earnings yield of ~4.65%, barely competitive with risk-free Indian government paper, and offers no cushion against the earnings volatility inherent to civil-construction/EPC contracting. A company incorporated in 2018 cannot possibly supply the 5–10 years of stable, growing earnings I require in "The Intelligent Investor." The absence of published P/B, current ratio, and debt figures is itself disqualifying — I cannot compute the Graham Number nor verify that the enterprise can survive a downturn, and in construction/EPC, working-capital crunches and receivable blow-ups are the historical killers.

The ROE of 23% and ROCE of 20.1% are genuinely attractive and I do not dismiss them, but these are recent, post-listing figures from a company riding a solar-policy tailwind — exactly the kind of "story" metric Mr. Market pays up for and that a prudent investor discounts heavily. Promoter holding at 58.34% is reassuring for alignment, but FII/DII interest is negligible (0.22% / 3.15%), confirming institutional skepticism. The rational course is to wait: let three to five years of audited results accumulate, observe how earnings behave through a solar capex cycle, and revisit only if Mr. Market offers the stock at a meaningful discount to tangible book with a P/E under 15. Until then, AVOID.
